status: Draft development questions proposed by the assistant; not user-reviewed, gold-labeled, or held-out evaluation data.

questions.question: My document assistant cites real papers but makes claims they do not support. Compare two approaches in this collection that could address this, explain what evidence each paper provides, and propose a small test for my project.

My retriever often returns passages that mention the topic but do not answer the question. How do Corrective RAG and Self-RAG respond to weak evidence, and which parts could I test without retraining my generator?

I have a limited inference budget. Compare always retrieving, deciding whether to retrieve, and iterative retrieval using the papers here. What measured evidence is available about the quality versus cost tradeoff?

For a small Qwen document agent, what does Search-R1 establish about training search behavior, and what does it leave untested about answering questions over AI research papers? Compare its setup with a prompting-based agent.

My agent answers questions from one passage but fails when a second search depends on the first result. Compare ReAct and Search-R1 as possible approaches and identify evidence relevant to this failure.

I currently reward short-answer overlap and citation IDs. What parts of Search-R1's reward setup could transfer to my agent, and why might that reward fail to measure faithful research explanations? Separate paper findings from your inference.
Before I pay for RL training, what prompting or retrieval baselines should I implement? Use at least two papers to justify the comparison and explain which variables should be held fixed.
Can I conclude that Search-R1 is better than Self-RAG for my project by comparing their reported headline scores? Inspect their experimental settings and explain which comparisons are justified.

I want the assistant to say it lacks evidence instead of guessing. Which papers here evaluate behavior relevant to that goal, and what additional test would I need before claiming fewer unsupported answers?

Which approaches in this collection let me refresh external knowledge without retraining all model weights? Compare at least two and distinguish updating a corpus from teaching the model to use retrieval.

What is the latest research on reducing unsupported claims in tool-using research agents? State the dates and limits of this collection, identify relevant approaches it contains, and explain what further search is needed.
Does this collection establish that retrieval eliminates hallucinations? Compare the evidence from at least two papers and distinguish improved benchmark performance from a guarantee.

My private-document project cannot send queries to public web search. Compare which components of Corrective RAG and Search-R1 could operate against a local corpus and identify any assumptions you cannot verify.

What evidence in these papers is directly relevant to a model around 7B parameters, and what conclusions rely on a different model size or setup? Recommend a baseline with explicit evidence limitations.
My users ask both simple fact questions and multi-step comparisons. How does Adaptive-RAG choose a strategy, how does that differ from Self-RAG, and what would I measure to see whether routing helps?
Why does Search-R1 mask retrieved tokens during training? Explain the supported rationale and how that differs from changing the document retrieval method.

I only have abstracts for some papers. Which recommendations about training cost and implementation can this collection actually support, and which require full methods, tables, or code? Give concrete examples.

How should I test whether training improves evidence gathering rather than memorizing answers? Use the experimental designs in at least two papers to motivate a held-out evaluation for my paper assistant.

Which method in this collection is guaranteed to fit on a single 24GB GPU and answer in under two seconds? Check whether the papers substantiate those exact constraints and explain what profiling is still required.

Given a small document agent that sometimes searches badly and sometimes exaggerates evidence, choose one first intervention from this collection. Compare it with an alternative, cite the relevant evidence, and define a result that would make you abandon the intervention.
